trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Barcelona
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Barcelona Airport around 13:00. Take the Aerobus or Metro L9 Sud (budget-friendly, ~€5.50) to the Eixample district. Check in to Barcelona Boutique Stay, freshen up, and take a relaxed walk along Passeig de Gràcia to admire the famous Modernista facades including Casa Batlló and Casa Milà (La Pedrera) from the outside — free to view exteriors. Pick up a city map and orient yourself with the iconic grid layout of Eixample.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll to the nearby Rambla de Catalunya for a lively early evening atmosphere. Explore the Eixample neighborhood streets and enjoy the warm August evening. Head to a local bar for a classic Catalan 'vermut' (vermouth) hour around 19:00 — very affordable and authentic.

meals.breakfast: Grab a coffee and croissant at the airport or skip — arrival is at 13:00
meals.lunch: Pick up a fresh bocadillo (sandwich) or slice of pizza from a local bakery or supermarket near the hotel for under €5 as a quick post-arrival meal
meals.dinner: Cervecería Catalana on Carrer de Mallorca — a beloved local spot with affordable tapas (patatas bravas, pan con tomate, croquetas). Budget ~€12–15 per person including a drink

day_by_day.notes: August in Barcelona is hot (28–33°C typically). Pack light clothing, sunscreen, and a reusable water bottle. Public fountains provide free drinking water. Validate your Metro ticket or get a T-Casual 10-trip card (~€11.35) for the best transport value all week.

day_by_day.morning: Start the day early (before the heat peaks) with a visit to the iconic Sagrada Família. Book tickets online in advance to save time and get the best price (~€26 standard entry). Spend 2–2.5 hours exploring Gaudí's masterpiece, including the towers for panoramic city views. The basilica is a 15-minute walk or short Metro ride from Eixample.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take a short Metro ride to Park Güell. The monumental zone requires a timed ticket (~€10 booked online) — the surrounding free park area is also worth exploring. Enjoy the mosaic terraces, Gaudí's architectural whimsy, and sweeping views over Barcelona. Afterward, head back toward Gràcia neighborhood and wander its charming plazas and independent boutiques.
day_by_day.evening: As the sun sets, head to El Born / Gothic Quarter (reachable by Metro, ~20 min). Explore the narrow medieval streets and discover hidden plazas. Join the local nightlife scene — Barcelona comes alive after 22:00. Start with drinks at a budget bar in El Born (many offer €3–4 beers) before deciding whether to extend the night at a club.

meals.breakfast: Grab a coffee with toast and tomato (pa amb tomàquet) at a neighborhood café near the hotel — classic Catalan breakfast for ~€3–4
meals.lunch: Look for a 'Menú del Día' (set lunch menu) near Park Güell or Gràcia — typically €10–13 for starter, main, dessert, bread, and a drink. Excellent value
meals.dinner: El Xampanyet in El Born — a legendary cava bar with affordable tapas and house cava. Budget ~€10–15 per person

day_by_day.notes: Book Sagrada Família and Park Güell tickets online at least a few days in advance — they often sell out, especially in August. Arrive at Park Güell at your earliest timed slot to avoid peak heat and crowds.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Gothic Quarter (Barri Gòtic) in depth — it's free to wander. Visit the Barcelona Cathedral (free entry before 12:30 and after 17:30 on weekdays), the Plaça Reial, and the ancient Roman ruins visible through glass floors in the Museu d'Història de Barcelona (MUHBA, ~€7, free first Sunday of month). Lose yourself in the labyrinthine medieval streets.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to La Barceloneta beach (free entry) for a few hours of sun and sea — a perfect August afternoon activity. The beach is reachable by Metro (Barceloneta station) or a scenic 20-minute walk from the Gothic Quarter along the waterfront. Rent a sun lounger (~€6) or simply use your towel on the sand. Explore the Port Olímpic area and the striking Frank Gehry Fish sculpture.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the Eixample area and explore the 'Gayxample' neighborhood for vibrant pre-night drinks. Barcelona's nightlife truly starts late — dinner at 21:00, drinks from 23:00, clubs from midnight onwards. Check out Carrer del Consell de Cent and surrounding streets for affordable cocktail bars. For architecture lovers, many buildings are dramatically lit at night — a free evening walking tour of illuminated Modernista buildings is worthwhile.

meals.breakfast: Forn de Sant Jaume bakery or similar near the hotel — coffee and a pastry for ~€3
meals.lunch: Grab a fresh sandwich, fruit, and water from a Mercadona or Lidl supermarket (~€4–6 total) and eat on the beach — very budget-friendly
meals.dinner: La Cova Fumada in Barceloneta (cash only, arrives early — opens ~13:00 for lunch but check evening hours) or try Bar Electricitat for authentic local tapas. Budget €10–14 per person

day_by_day.notes: Beware of pickpockets in the Gothic Quarter and on Las Ramblas — keep bags secure. The beach gets very crowded in August; arrive by 10:00 for a good spot if planning a morning visit. Nightclubs in Barcelona typically charge €10–20 entry, sometimes including a drink.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Palau de la Música Catalana — a stunning UNESCO-listed Modernista concert hall by Lluís Domènech i Montaner. Guided tours run ~€22 but the exterior and lobby area give a taste for free. Then explore the El Born Cultural Centre (free entry to the archaeological site inside) and the surrounding trendy El Born neighborhood with its independent galleries and street art.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the Metro to Montjuïc (or the cable car for ~€12.70 return for a splurge). Visit the free Jardins de Laribal and Jardí Botànic views, the Fundació Joan Miró (~€14, worth it for art lovers), and the Castell de Montjuïc (€5 entry, panoramic views over the city and port). The Olympic Stadium exterior is free to view. Spend 3–4 hours exploring this hilltop area.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the Eixample for a classic Barcelona evening. Visit the Mercat de l'Eixample or nearby local bars for pre-dinner drinks. After dinner, explore the live music scene — many bars in Eixample and Gràcia offer free live jazz or Catalan music on weekends. Check listings at Time Out Barcelona for free events. For nightlife, Sala Apolo in Poble Sec offers great music events (~€10–15 entry).

meals.breakfast: Bar Calders in Sant Antoni neighborhood — a beloved local café with excellent coffee and breakfast for ~€4–5
meals.lunch: Mercat de Sant Antoni (recently renovated market near Eixample) — fresh market stalls with affordable local food, ~€8–10 for a full meal
meals.dinner: Bodega Sepúlveda — a traditional Catalan wine bar and restaurant with affordable raciones (shared plates). Budget ~€12–16 per person with wine

day_by_day.notes: The Fundació Joan Miró offers free entry on Saturday afternoons after 15:00 — check current schedule to save on entry. Montjuïc Magic Fountain shows run Thursday–Sunday evenings in summer (free) — a spectacular light and water display worth catching if timing aligns.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning walk along Passeig de Gràcia to revisit favourite Modernista buildings and do any last-minute souvenir shopping. Visit the Mercat de la Boqueria on Las Ramblas (free entry — go early before crowds, ~09:00) to browse the colourful food stalls. Pick up local products like olive oil, saffron, or turron as affordable gifts. Alternatively, explore the less touristy Mercat de l'Abaceria in Gràcia for a more authentic experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure time, enjoy a final leisurely lunch in the Eixample. Pack bags and check out of the hotel. Take the Metro L9 Sud or Aerobus back to Barcelona Airport. Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight for check-in and security, especially in busy August.

meals.breakfast: Final café con leche and croissant at a local neighbourhood bar — ~€2.50–3.50. A quintessential Barcelona morning ritual
meals.lunch: Federal Café or similar brunch spot in Eixample for a relaxed final meal — budget €10–14. Alternatively, grab a bocadillo from a bakery for ~€4–5 if time is tight
meals.dinner: Airport or in-flight — pick up snacks from a supermarket before heading to the airport to avoid expensive airport food

day_by_day.notes: Check hotel checkout time (typically 11:00 or 12:00) and arrange luggage storage if your flight is later in the day — many hotels offer this for free. The T-Casual Metro card is valid for the airport Metro L9 line. Keep all receipts if you plan to claim VAT refunds on purchases over €90.15 (available to non-EU residents). Total estimated budget for 5 days excluding flights: ~€300–400 per person, covering accommodation, transport, entry fees, and meals.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 13:00. Travel from airport to Barcelona Boutique Stay in Eixample via Aerobus or Metro L9 Sud (approx. 35–45 min). Check in, freshen up, and get oriented in the neighborhood.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stroll the iconic Passeig de Gràcia boulevard right from your doorstep in Eixample. Admire the exterior facades of Casa Batlló and Casa Milà (La Pedrera) as a gentle introduction to Gaudí's Modernista architecture — no tickets needed for the outside views. Browse the elegant Eixample grid streets and get your bearings.
day_by_day.evening: Ease into Barcelona's late dining culture with dinner at a mid-range Eixample restaurant. Afterward, enjoy a leisurely walk along Passeig de Gràcia lit up at night — a beautiful and low-key first evening.

meals.breakfast: Skip or grab a light snack at the airport before landing.
meals.lunch: Grab a quick bocadillo or menú del día at a café near the hotel after check-in (budget ~€12–15).
meals.dinner: Cervecería Catalana on Carrer de Mallorca — beloved local spot for tapas and montaditos, mid-range pricing (~€25–35 per person). Arrive after 20:30 to dine like a local.

day_by_day.notes: August in Barcelona is hot (expect 28–33°C). Pack light clothing and stay hydrated. Keep Day 1 relaxed to recover from travel. Book Sagrada Família tickets online in advance if not already done — they sell out weeks ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Sagrada Família Guided Tour — Book the skip-the-line guided tour for a 9:00 or 10:00 entry slot (the basilica is just a 15-minute walk or short metro ride from Eixample). Spend 2–2.5 hours exploring the Nativity and Passion facades, the stunning interior nave, and the tower views. The guided tour adds rich context about Gaudí's vision and ongoing construction.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the hotel for a midday rest during peak heat (13:00–15:30). Then head to Park Güell & Gràcia Neighborhood Exploration — take the Metro or a short taxi to Park Güell. Visit the monumental zone with its mosaic dragon staircase and Hypostyle Room (timed ticket required, book ahead). Afterward, wander the charming bohemian streets of Gràcia village for boutique shopping and café culture.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy the sunset from the upper terraces of Park Güell if your ticket allows a late afternoon slot, then head back toward Eixample for dinner and a first taste of the city's nightlife scene.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a nearby Eixample bakery — try a croissant de mantequilla and café amb llet (~€5–8).
meals.lunch: Menú del día near Sagrada Família — a 3-course meal with wine for ~€13–16 at a local restaurant on Carrer de la Marina.
meals.dinner: La Pepita in Gràcia — creative pintxos and tapas in a beautifully tiled space, ~€20–30 per person. Pair with a glass of Catalan cava.

day_by_day.notes: Book Park Güell monumental zone tickets online (€10–13) — they sell out fast in August. Wear comfortable walking shoes. Sagrada Família towers require a separate ticket add-on — worth it for the views.

day_by_day.morning: Gothic Quarter & El Born Architecture Walk — Take the Metro to Jaume I and spend the morning on a self-guided or small-group walking tour. Explore the Roman walls, Barcelona Cathedral, Plaça Reial, and the narrow medieval laneways of the Barri Gòtic. Cross into El Born to see the stunning Santa Maria del Mar basilica and the trendy boutique-lined streets.
day_by_day.afternoon: La Barceloneta Beach & Seafood Experience — From El Born it's a 15-minute walk to Barceloneta beach. Spend the hottest part of the afternoon swimming and relaxing on Barcelona's most famous urban beach. Rent a sun lounger (~€6–8) and soak up the Mediterranean atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Dine at a traditional chiringuito (beach bar-restaurant) on the Barceloneta seafront for fresh seafood as the sun sets over the water. Then head back toward Eixample for a nightcap.

meals.breakfast: Federal Café in El Born — excellent brunch spot popular with locals, avocado toast or eggs (~€10–14).
meals.lunch: Light snack or bocadillo from a Barceloneta kiosk on the beach (~€6–10) to keep energy up for swimming.
meals.dinner: La Cova Fumada or La Mar Salada near Barceloneta — traditional Catalan seafood, fresh grilled fish and paella, ~€30–40 per person. Reserve ahead for August.

day_by_day.notes: Barceloneta gets extremely crowded in August — arrive by 15:00 to secure a good spot. Watch your belongings on the beach. The Gothic Quarter is best explored on foot; comfortable sandals recommended. Santa Maria del Mar has free entry in the mornings.

day_by_day.morning: Dedicate the morning to deeper Eixample Modernisme exploration — visit the interior of Casa Batlló or La Pedrera (Casa Milà), both steps from your hotel. La Pedrera's rooftop with its warrior-chimney sculptures is iconic and opens at 9:00. The Magic Nights rooftop event runs in summer evenings, but the daytime visit is equally stunning. Choose one for a 2-hour immersive visit (~€25–28 per person).
day_by_day.afternoon: Relaxed afternoon for personal exploration — browse the Mercat de l'Abaceria in Gràcia or the Mercat de Sant Antoni in Eixample (a stunning renovated 19th-century iron market) for local produce, vintage finds, and café culture. Return to the hotel to rest and prepare for the big night out.
day_by_day.evening: Eixample Modernista Bar Crawl & Nightlife — Start the evening with cocktails at architecturally stunning Art Nouveau bars in Eixample (try Dry Martini Bar or Bar Calders). Progress to the Eixample Esquerra 'Gayxample' area for a vibrant bar-hopping scene, then head to a club like Sala Apolo or Razzmatazz later in the night. Barcelona nightlife starts late — clubs peak after 01:00.

meals.breakfast: Hofmann Pastisseria in Eixample — legendary pastry school bakery, incredible croissants and pastries (~€6–10).
meals.lunch: Mercat de Sant Antoni food stalls — graze on local cheeses, charcuterie, and fresh juice (~€12–18).
meals.dinner: Bodega Sepúlveda — cozy Eixample wine bar with excellent Catalan dishes and natural wines, ~€25–35 per person. Dine at 21:00 to fuel the night ahead.

day_by_day.notes: Book La Pedrera or Casa Batlló tickets online to avoid queues. For the bar crawl, pace yourself — Barcelona nightlife is a marathon, not a sprint. Clubs often have free entry before 01:00 with a flyer or guest list. Dress smart-casual for most venues.

day_by_day.morning: Slow, relaxed morning to recover from the night out — sleep in and enjoy a late breakfast. Spend a final quiet hour packing and checking out of the hotel (or storing luggage at reception). Take one last walk along Passeig de Gràcia to pick up any souvenirs — artisan shops and design stores abound in Eixample.
day_by_day.afternoon: Final afternoon exploration — visit the Fundació Antoni Tàpies in Eixample (housed in a stunning Modernista building, ~€12 entry) for a dose of Catalan contemporary art and architecture combined. Alternatively, revisit a favorite neighborhood café or rooftop bar for a final view of the city skyline.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner in Eixample before any late departures or a final night in the city. Reflect on the trip over a glass of local Priorat red wine and traditional Catalan cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Late brunch at Parking Pizza or Flax & Kale in Eixample — healthy, generous portions, great coffee (~€14–18).
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a rooftop bar or terrace restaurant in Eixample with city views (~€18–25).
meals.dinner: Moments or a classic Catalan restaurant like Can Culleretes (oldest restaurant in Barcelona, in the Gothic Quarter) for a memorable farewell meal — ~€30–45 per person.

day_by_day.notes: If departing by air, allow 2.5–3 hours before flight time to reach El Prat airport from central Barcelona in August traffic. Store luggage at the hotel or at Barcelona Sants station if needed. Consider buying a bottle of local cava or Catalan olive oil as a take-home gift from the Mercat de Sant Antoni.

Take a leisurely self-guided stroll along Passeig de Gràcia to admire the iconic Modernista facades of the Block of Discord — Casa Batlló, Casa Amatller, and Casa Lleó Morera — all within walking distance of the hotel. Consider purchasing timed-entry tickets on the spot or via app for Casa Batlló's illuminated evening experience.
day_by_day.evening: Begin your Barcelona nightlife initiation with cocktails at a rooftop bar in Eixample — Dry Martini or Bar Calders are quintessential upscale choices. Follow with a late dinner at a celebrated Eixample restaurant, easing into the Spanish rhythm of dining after 21:00.

meals.breakfast: Enjoy a welcome snack or coffee at the hotel upon arrival — no formal breakfast scheduled given the midday arrival.
meals.lunch: Light bite near the airport or upon settling in: grab a premium sandwich and coffee at Federal Café in Eixample, a sophisticated local favourite.
meals.dinner: Disfrutar (2 Michelin stars) or Cinc Sentits — both are world-class tasting-menu restaurants in Eixample offering avant-garde Catalan cuisine; book well in advance.

day_by_day.notes: Arrange a private airport transfer ahead of time for a seamless luxury arrival. Confirm hotel early check-in if possible. Keep the afternoon relaxed to recover from travel. Purchase skip-the-line tickets for Sagrada Família online tonight for Day 2.

day_by_day.morning: Sagrada Família Guided Tour — Join a premium skip-the-line guided tour of Gaudí's awe-inspiring basilica, including tower access for panoramic views over Barcelona. Allocate 2–2.5 hours to fully absorb the Nativity and Passion facades, the luminous interior nave, and the museum crypt. The earlier morning slot (9:00–9:30) is ideal to beat the midday crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Park Güell & Gràcia Neighborhood Exploration — Take a short taxi or ride-share to Park Güell. Explore the mosaic terraces, the dragon staircase, Gaudí's whimsical Hypostyle Room, and enjoy sweeping panoramic views of the city. Afterward, descend into the charming Gràcia neighborhood for a relaxed wander through its bohemian plazas and independent boutiques.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Eixample and prepare for an elegant evening. Enjoy pre-dinner cocktails at the Mandarin Oriental's Banker's Bar on Passeig de Gràcia, then head to dinner at a top-tier restaurant before a sophisticated nightcap at a jazz or cocktail lounge.

meals.breakfast: Lavish hotel breakfast or visit Forn de Sant Josep, an exquisite Eixample bakery-café, for artisan pastries, fresh orange juice, and specialty coffee.
meals.lunch: Alfresco lunch in Gràcia — La Pepita or Parking Pizza (gourmet) for a relaxed, high-quality midday meal with natural wines.
meals.dinner: Lasarte (3 Michelin stars, Eixample) — the pinnacle of Barcelona fine dining with Basque-Catalan haute cuisine by chef Martín Berasategui.

day_by_day.notes: Book Sagrada Família tower access well in advance as slots sell out weeks ahead. Park Güell's Monumental Zone also requires timed-entry tickets — purchase online. Wear comfortable shoes for the Park Güell hillside terrain.

day_by_day.morning: Gothic Quarter & El Born Architecture Walk — Join a premium small-group guided walking tour through Barcelona's medieval Gothic Quarter. Discover hidden Roman ruins, the magnificent Barcelona Cathedral, Plaça Reial, and the atmospheric labyrinthine streets. Cross into the adjacent El Born district to admire the stunning iron-and-glass Mercat de Santa Caterina and the Basílica de Santa Maria del Mar, a masterpiece of Catalan Gothic architecture.
day_by_day.afternoon: La Barceloneta Beach & Seafood Experience — Head to Barceloneta for a premium beach afternoon. Rent a private sunbed and parasol at a beach club such as Pacha Beach Club or Eclipse at W Barcelona. Soak in the Mediterranean sun before transitioning to a traditional chiringuito or upscale beachfront restaurant for a long, indulgent seafood lunch-into-afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Eixample Modernista Bar Crawl & Nightlife — Experience Barcelona's legendary nightlife with a curated Art Nouveau bar crawl starting in Eixample. Begin at architecturally stunning cocktail bars, progress through the vibrant Eixample Esquerra (Gayxample) scene, and finish at an exclusive club such as Sutton, Otto Zutz, or Pacha Barcelona for a full luxury nightlife experience.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or visit Caravelle café in El Raval for specialty third-wave coffee and avocado toast before the morning tour.
meals.lunch: La Mar Salada or Barraca — upscale beachfront restaurants in Barceloneta celebrated for premium paella, fresh grilled seafood, and panoramic sea views.
meals.dinner: Late tapas dinner at El Xampanyet in El Born (classic, beloved cava bar with exceptional pintxos) or Bar del Pla for refined modern Catalan tapas before the nightlife crawl.

day_by_day.notes: The Gothic Quarter is best explored on foot with a knowledgeable guide to uncover hidden courtyards and layers of history. Barceloneta gets very crowded in August — arrive at the beach club by 14:00 to secure premium spots. For the bar crawl, dress smartly — Barcelona's top venues enforce a stylish dress code.

day_by_day.morning: Deeper Modernisme Immersion — Spend the morning visiting Casa Batlló (Passeig de Gràcia, steps from the hotel) with the premium Magic Nights or full multimedia guided experience, one of the most theatrical architectural tours in the world. Alternatively, visit the equally spectacular Casa Milà (La Pedrera) rooftop for its surreal chimneys and wraparound city views. Both are Gaudí masterpieces and UNESCO World Heritage Sites.
day_by_day.afternoon: Palau de la Música Catalana & El Born Luxury Shopping — Visit the Palau de la Música Catalana, Lluís Domènech i Montaner's breathtaking Modernista concert hall (guided tour or attend a rehearsal concert if available). Afterward, explore El Born's luxury boutiques and concept stores — Custo Barcelona, independent jewellery designers, and artisan leather goods — for premium souvenir shopping.
day_by_day.evening: Montjuïc Sunset & Exclusive Dinner — Take a private car or cable car up to Montjuïc for golden-hour views over the city and port. Visit the Fundació Joan Miró if time permits. Descend for a refined dinner in the Poble Sec neighbourhood — one of Barcelona's most exciting emerging dining districts — before a nightcap in Eixample.

meals.breakfast: Brunch at Cosmo or Syra Coffee in Eixample — stylish, high-quality brunch spots beloved by locals and design-conscious travellers.
meals.lunch: Bar Calders or Bodega Sepúlveda in Eixample Esquerra for a relaxed, wine-forward lunch with excellent Catalan charcuterie and cheese boards.
meals.dinner: Tickets (Albert Adrià's avant-garde tapas bar in Poble Sec) — one of the most creative and coveted dining experiences in Barcelona; reservations open 60 days in advance and are essential.

day_by_day.notes: Book Palau de la Música Catalana guided tours in advance. The Montjuïc cable car (Telefèric de Montjuïc) is a scenic experience but can have queues — a private car or taxi is a seamless luxury alternative. Tickets restaurant reservations are notoriously difficult; set a calendar reminder for the 60-day booking window.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely Eixample Morning & Farewell Exploration — Enjoy a slow, indulgent final morning. Stroll the elegant boulevards of Eixample, browse the Mercat de l'Abaceria or Mercat de l'Eixample for artisan food products as gifts. Visit any remaining architectural gems — the Hospital de Sant Pau (another Domènech i Montaner UNESCO masterpiece, a 10-minute walk from the hotel) is a hidden gem compared to the more touristed Gaudí sites and is unmissable for architecture lovers.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last Afternoon at Leisure & Pre-Departure Preparation — Return to the hotel for a final lunch and to collect luggage. Allow ample time for a private transfer to the airport. Alternatively, if the flight departs late, spend a final afternoon at a luxury spa — the Mandarin Oriental Spa or the Grand Hotel Central Spa offer world-class treatments ideal for pre-flight relaxation.
day_by_day.evening: Departure — Transfer to Barcelona El Prat Airport (BCN). Enjoy access to the premium lounge before your flight.

meals.breakfast: Final luxurious hotel breakfast — request a special spread or champagne breakfast as a farewell treat from the boutique hotel.
meals.lunch: Cervecería Catalana on Carrer Mallorca — an Eixample institution famous for its exceptional montaditos, craft beers, and buzzing atmosphere; perfect for a final relaxed lunch steps from the hotel.
meals.dinner: Airport lounge dining or a light pre-flight meal — alternatively, if departing late evening, a farewell dinner at Moments (Mandarin Oriental, 2 Michelin stars) for an unforgettable final Barcelona meal.

day_by_day.notes: Hospital de Sant Pau is significantly less crowded than Gaudí's sites and equally stunning — a perfect final-morning discovery. Arrange private airport transfer in advance. Barcelona traffic can be heavy in August afternoons — allow at least 60–75 minutes to reach the airport from Eixample. Pick up premium Catalan wines, olive oils, or artisan chocolates as gifts at Vila Viniteca in El Born or Colmado Quilez in Eixample.
